5gok:
The Bachelor of Counselling provides students with a comprehensive and flexible approach to theoretical, experiential, and skills-based learning. Students will learn strategies to successfully explore a career in contemporary counselling, including how to support individuals, couples, families, or groups, considering the cultural and social-political context in which they live and how this may affect them. The course is delivered in small group environments on-campus, online and by blended delivery (nine counselling units) by well-qualified and experienced academic teachers using quality curriculum.

This course is accredited by the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA) and the Australian Counselling Association (ACA).
5gow:
The Bachelor of Criminology and Justice gives students deep insight into why we behave the way we do, and the effect our justice system has on our future actions.

The course enables students to understand our criminal justice system and its relationship to the community. Students have the opportunity to get inside the minds of criminals to understand the reasons behind criminal behaviour and how criminal law and social control fit into our justice system.
5gom:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science gives students deep insight into why people think and act the way they do, with an understanding of the connection between an individual, society and culture. Begin their studies by exploring key foundational psychological processes and how these can be applied in a professional context, before diving deeper into cognition, lifespan development, and biological bases. Examine abnormal psychology and intervention strategies, individual differences and assessment, and social and community psychology. Develop their clinical speciality by studying elective units across psychology, counselling, criminology and social welfare. Explore psychology as it relates to crime and justice, delve into the world of forensic psychology, enhance your trauma-informed counselling skills, or discover your passion for social work and community welfare.

This course is conditionally accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.
5gpb:
Program Description

The Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours delivers an advanced level of psychological knowledge, research and writing skills.

This one-year degree provides students the fourth year of accredited study in psychology, perfect if they have already completed three years of accredited study and want to train to work as a registered psychologist in Australia.

This course includes an individual 12,000-word thesis.
7v15:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science and Counselling is specialised course that gives students the skills to successfully explore a career in counselling and applied psychology. The program gives students a deep insight into why we think and act the way we do, what impact society has on our actions, and how to empower people to act differently. Included in this course is industry placement and counselling client contact, giving them the hands-on experience ACAP is known for.

This course is accredited by the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA). It is also accredited by ACAP under its self-accrediting authority.
6ui0:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science and Criminology course is a specialised double major degree, ideal if the student is interested in working in the courts, corrections, youth justice or with offenders, victims or vulnerable populations including young people and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. The program gives students deep insight into why we think and act the way we do, and how to help change behaviour before it becomes destructive, or rehabilitate those who have already progressed down a path of crime.

This course has been accredited by ACAP under its self-accrediting authority.
5gor:
A Bachelor of Social Work in Australia is a professionally accredited four-year undergraduate degree. Throughout their studies, the students will develop practical skills and applicable knowledge across a range of compelling subject areas, including social work theory and practice, advanced mental health awareness, lifespan development and foundational psychological processes. Tailoring this degree to their interests by exploring elective units such as family and relationship counselling, addictive behaviours counselling, mental health and criminal justice, and life coaching. This program helps students to graduate with 1,000 hours of applied social work practice, ready to hit the ground running in mental health, community welfare, women and migrant services, or corrections and justice.

This course is accredited by the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA) and the Australian Counselling Association (ACA).
8w1c:
ACAP’s professionally accredited Master of Professional Accounting (MPA) is designed to equip graduates with advanced knowledge and skills for a successful career in the accounting profession. The program develops professional capabilities across key areas including management accounting, financial reporting, economics, data analysis, and company law, while fostering critical and innovative thinking to address real-world problems ethically, with strong awareness of corporate governance and social responsibility.

The course comprises 12 units aligned with the competency areas of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ) and CPA Australia (CPA), along with four elective units in either small to medium business management or business management and administration. The MPA fulfils the academic requirements of CPA Australia and CAANZ, with accreditation signifying that the program meets the highest professional standards in accounting.

The program also incorporates a work-integrated learning unit as the culmination of study, providing opportunities to apply knowledge in a practical setting through a work placement or an industry-focused project.
5gpf:
The Master of Professional Psychology continues the student's deep understanding of human behaviour, and is the fifth year of the six years' professional training required for general registration as a psychologist in Australia.

Students can then complete a one-year Psychology Board of Australia approved internship or the Graduate Diploma of Professional Psychological Practice to have the fifth and sixth years of training required for general registration as a psychologist.

This course is conditionally accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC).
5gpg:
The Master of Psychology (Clinical) continues the student's deep understanding of human behaviour and mental health. This is the fifth and sixth year sequence of professional training in psychology for general registration as a psychologist in Australia.

The aim of the Master of Psychology (Clinical) program is to equip graduates with the knowledge, skills, attributes and competencies to be able to undertake professional practice in a range of clinical settings with diverse client populations.

The Master of Psychology (Clinical) has been developed in alignment with Psychological Sciences’ educational philosophy that aims to provide students with comprehensive evidence-based theoretical and practical learning and with close reference to the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council Rules for Accreditation and Accreditation Standards for Psychology Courses (January 2019 Standards) and the Psychology Board of Australian General Registration Standard.

The course includes coursework and independent research leading to a thesis and practical placement. It also has a minimum 1,000 hours of practical skills and training at our on-campus clinic and external locations. This course is conditionally accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC).
7v32:
The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) delivers a comprehensive understanding of the reasons behind human thoughts and behaviour, as well as the essential skills and knowledge to enhance student's role as a Social Worker. Throughout the degree, students will study social work as a profession, including its history, ethics and key influences. Informed by principles of social justice and human rights, students will develop an understanding of the social work practice methods required to work effectively and ethically with a wide range of service users in diverse contexts.

The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) program will strengthen students skills in critical thinking and analysis, anti-oppressive practice, community empowerment, systemic advocacy, cultural sensitivity, and social research. Students will also have the opportunity to integrate their classroom learning with professional practice through placement opportunities and supervision, totalling 1000 hours of practical work experience.

This is an Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) accredited qualification. The Navitas Professional Institute (NPI) has also accredited the Master of Social Work (Qualifying) course under its self-accrediting authority.
8lxj: Master of Business Administration (MBA) combines the human-focused knowledge students need with the in-demand skills employers want – it’s the MBA with a side of TLC. With a 40-year history of delivering tertiary education courses in applied psychology, this course delves into the traits needed to become an exceptional leader, fostering both soft skills – such as empathy, self-awareness, resilience, negotiation, flexibility, and emotional intelligence – and technical skills to produce well-rounded, career-ready graduates.
